Subject: Renewal conversation + Q on burst top-up

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the usage export earlier. We're two months out from our renewal and the team is seeing repeated midweek surges that make it hard to keep latency under 450ms for interactive features. We want to avoid committing a large tranche if the extra GPUs won't actually be used most of the quarter.

Is there a way to do a staged top-up tied to the snapshot you shared, or a short-term burst that only bills when used? Also curious whether Redwood can provide a short SLO impact simulation if we add 8 GPUs vs 16 GPUs.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + Q on burst top-up

Elena —

Appreciate the detail and good call flagging midweek tail spikes. Short answer: yes — we can structure a renewal that stages capacity and ties top-ups to observed snapshot thresholds. High-level proposal attached: a two-stage top-up with a 60-day observation window and built-in rollback.

Quick outline:
- Stage A (30 days after renewal): add 8 GPUs to the dedicated pool (reserved) for baseline surge smoothing.
- Stage B (automatic, day 61): evaluate utilization and if 95th percentile weeklong queueing/latency metrics exceed the threshold, automatically allocate an additional 8 GPUs (total +16).
- Billing: Stage A is reserved monthly commit; Stage B converts to reserved only after the stage completes 30 days in the auto-rollup state. Until then, Stage B capacity is billed as burst usage at lower commitment price (metered).

I've asked Ben to run a quick SLO sensitivity sim against the CSV you attached so we can show likely p99 impact for +8 and +16 variants. Also adding Dev to this thread for confirmation on operational rollout and canary routing.

Next step: I'll send the formal amendment (proposed_topup_amendment_v1.pdf) and the SLO sensitivity workbook by end of day. If that looks good, we can target a June 30 renewal signature and July 1 Stage A activation.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 11:03 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I've asked Ben to run a quick SLO sensitivity sim against the CSV you attached so we can show likely p99 impact for +8 and +16 variants.

Attached the SLO sensitivity workbook (slo-impact-sensitivity.xlsx) with modeled p50/p95/p99 token latency across the three scenarios: current, +8 reserved, +16 reserved. High-level results: +8 reduces p99 by ~28% during peak windows; +16 reduces by ~42% but with diminishing returns after +12 GPUs for your observed spike distribution.

Operational notes for Dev: we recommend enabling prefix KV cache for your 4 heaviest endpoints prior to Stage A activation; that will lower the effective load and reduce the chance Stage B triggers. If Ops wants, we can scope a one-week canary (20% traffic) routed to the new tranche for safety.

Also — for renewals where customers request staged top-ups we normally offer a one-time goodwill credit equal to 25% of Stage A's first month to offset switching friction. Value available if Lumina signs before June 30.

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Elena —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Ben's workbook, +8 looks like the sweet spot to remove most of your tail pain at lower incremental committed cost. Proposed next steps:

1) We attach the proposed amendment (v1) with Stage A (8 GPUs) + automatic Stage B logic.
2) Lumina signs the amendment and we provision Stage A on July 1 (reserved commit).
3) We run a 14-day canary at 20% traffic starting July 2 to validate routing and prefix cache behavior; we will not convert Stage B to reserved until the 30-day auto-eval completes.
4) Apply a one-time credit for Stage A equal to 25% of first-month Stage A commit as a sign-by-June-30 incentive.

Please confirm acceptance of the outlined flow and I will circulate a DocuSign link for the amendment and schedule a kickoff with Dev and our infra team. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer.
